assumptions.condition: The variables \(Z_{ai}\) are mutually independent with \(Z_{ai}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(d_i)\).

definitions.name: Feasible product-dosage class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal D_L=\{d\in[0,1]^p: \sum_{i=1}^p d_i\le L\}\), with every index \(i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\).

definitions.name: Fixed low-order Fourier features
definitions.construction: \(\phi(x)=(\prod_{i\in S}x_i)_{S\in\mathcal I_k}\), with the empty product equal to one.

definitions.name: Population information and criterion
definitions.construction: \(\Sigma_k(d)=\mathbb E_d[\phi(X_a)\phi(X_a)^{\mathsf T}]\); set \(\Phi_k(d)=\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_k(d)^{-1})\) when \(\Sigma_k(d)\) is invertible and \(\Phi_k(d)=+\infty\) otherwise.

definitions.name: Known-information spectral-threshold OLS
definitions.construction: Form \(H_n(\varepsilon)=\Sigma_k(d^\star)^{-1/2}(F^{\mathsf T}F/n)\Sigma_k(d^\star)^{-1/2}-I_q\); on \(G_n(\varepsilon)=\{\|H_n(\varepsilon)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\varepsilon\}\), set \(\widehat\beta_{\varepsilon}=(F^{\mathsf T}F)^{-1}F^{\mathsf T}Y\), and set it to zero on the complement.

definitions.name: Finite-risk saddle handle
definitions.construction: Permutation-symmetrize the exact finite-support law of \(F^{\mathsf T}F\), retain the coefficient-ball spectral-fallback bias, and solve the resulting dosage-versus-coefficient saddle problem.

statements.statement: For every \(d\in\mathcal D_L\cap(0,1)^p\), the population Gram matrix is positive definite and \[\Phi_k(d)=\sum_{T\in\mathcal I_k}\prod_{i\in T}r(d_i)=\sum_{j=0}^{k}e_j(r(d_1),\ldots,r(d_p)).\] If any coordinate of \(d\) equals zero or one, then \(\Sigma_k(d)\) is singular and \(\Phi_k(d)=+\infty\). The interior identity is obtained by the triangular change from the fixed monomials to product-orthonormal features and is the Bernoulli specialization of the downward-closed product-design identity of Schwabe and Wong.
statements.justification: This representation removes the higher-order characteristic-polynomial obstruction and exposes separable curvature.
statements.gap: SchwabeWong1999 contains the general identity, while ShyamalZhangUhler2025 does not specialize it to solve the shared-supply all-order problem.
statements.consumer: The identity turns the interaction-design problem into an explicit scalar symmetric-polynomial optimization usable by the dosage theorem.

statements.statement: The unique minimizer of \(\Phi_k(d)\) over \(d\in\mathcal D_L\) is \(d^\star=u\mathbf 1_p\), where \(u=\min\{L/p,1/2\}\), and \[\Phi^\star=\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom pj r(u)^j.\] Moreover, every \(d\in\mathcal D_L\) satisfies \[\Phi_k(d)-\Phi^\star\ge 8C_{p,k}\|d-d^\star\|_2^2.\] The coefficient \(8C_{p,k}\) is the best global strong-convexity certificate when \(L\ge p/2\).
statements.justification: This is the exact design choice and a quantitative certificate of the loss from dosage imbalance.
statements.gap: ShyamalZhangUhler2025 proves the limited-supply closed form only for \(k=1\); SchwabeWong1999 does not impose or optimize the shared expected-supply simplex.
statements.consumer: An independent-delivery interaction screen can set all dosages to \(u\) and quantify the population precision penalty of implementation error.

statements.statement: At the optimal dosage, the exact maximum whitened leverage is \[\mu^\star=\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom pj\left(\frac{1-u}{u}\right)^j.\]
statements.justification: The leverage is the exact concentration scale of the whitened empirical Gram matrix.
statements.gap: Generic bounded-design analyses use dimension-dependent envelopes and do not compute this supply-sensitive Boolean leverage.
statements.consumer: The expression gives an explicit sample-size diagnostic before running a sparse-supply interaction experiment.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(T\in\mathcal I_k\) with \( |T|=k\), if no sampled unit has \(Z_{ai}=1\) for all \(i\in T\), then \(F\) is rank deficient. Consequently, under \(d^\star\), \[\mathbb P_{d^\star}(\operatorname{rank}(F)<q)\ge(1-u^k)^n.\]
statements.justification: This discrete null vector proves that rare joint activations are a necessary obstacle, not an artifact of matrix concentration.
statements.gap: HsuKakadeZhang2014 treats generic random-design conditioning and does not exploit Boolean activation polynomials.
statements.consumer: The bound warns a screen designer when a proposed sample size cannot reliably identify all \(k\)-fold coefficients.

statements.statement: Under \(d^\star\), let \(b_{n,\varepsilon}=\mathbb P_{d^\star}(G_n(\varepsilon)^c)\). On \(G_n(\varepsilon)\), \(\operatorname{Cov}(\widehat\beta_{\varepsilon}\mid F)=\sigma^2(F^{\mathsf T}F)^{-1}\), and \[\frac{\sigma^2}{n(1+\varepsilon)}\Sigma_k(d^\star)^{-1}\preceq\operatorname{Cov}(\widehat\beta_{\varepsilon}\mid F)\preceq\frac{\sigma^2}{n(1-\varepsilon)}\Sigma_k(d^\star)^{-1}.\] Unconditionally, \[R_n(\beta,\sigma,\varepsilon)=\sigma^2\mathbb E_{d^\star}\left[\mathbf 1_{G_n(\varepsilon)}\operatorname{tr}((F^{\mathsf T}F)^{-1})\right]+\|\beta\|_2^2b_{n,\varepsilon}.\] Furthermore, \(b_{n,\varepsilon}\le\min\{1,\delta_{n,\varepsilon}\}\), where \(\delta_{n,\varepsilon}=2q\exp\{-n\varepsilon^2/(3\mu^\star)\}\), and \[\frac{\sigma^2\Phi^\star}{n}\frac{1-b_{n,\varepsilon}}{1+\varepsilon}\le R_n(\beta,\sigma,\varepsilon)\le\frac{\sigma^2\Phi^\star}{n(1-\varepsilon)}+B^2b_{n,\varepsilon}.\] The upper bound also implies \[R_n(\beta,\sigma,\varepsilon)\le\frac{\sigma^2\Phi^\star}{n}(1+2\varepsilon)+2B^2q\exp\{-n\varepsilon^2/(3\mu^\star)\}.\]
statements.justification: The theorem verifies the exact Chernoff constant and keeps the fallback bias in the unconditional risk.
statements.gap: Tropp2012 supplies the tail tool and HsuKakadeZhang2014 supplies general decompositions, but neither gives this product-Fourier leverage calibration or fallback branch.
statements.consumer: The bound converts the exact population design into an auditable finite-sample precision guarantee.

statements.statement: For the threshold sequence \(\varepsilon_n=3\sqrt{\mu^\star\log(n)/n}\), with \(p,k,L,B,\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}\) fixed, \[\sup_{\substack{\|\beta\|_2\le B,\;\sigma\in[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]\\ \text{admissible conditional-noise laws}}}\left|\frac{R_n(\beta,\sigma,\varepsilon_n)}{\sigma^2\Phi^\star/n}-1\right|\longrightarrow0.\]
statements.justification: This establishes that the exact population \(A\)-risk is attained uniformly over the stated fixed-dimensional coefficient and noise class.
statements.gap: PFED gives near-optimal passive-risk control, whereas this statement isolates the all-order limited-supply oracle constant and its exact leverage-dependent threshold.
statements.consumer: The result justifies replacing numerical population design search by the uniform dosage in sufficiently large independent-delivery screens.

statements.statement: When \(k=1\), the criterion reduces to \(\Phi_1(d)=1+\sum_{i=1}^p r(d_i)\), and the optimizer reduces to the uniform limited-supply dosage in the additive PFED setting. When \(L\ge p/2\), it further reduces to half dosage with \(\Phi^\star=1+p\).
statements.justification: This is the required sanity reduction to the known additive and unconstrained designs.
statements.gap: The reduction is known from ShyamalZhangUhler2025; it is included as a fidelity check rather than a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: Readers can verify that the all-order theorem preserves the established additive benchmark.

statements.statement: Using the finite-risk saddle handle, characterize the dosage in \(\mathcal D_L\) minimizing the worst-case unconditional risk of the specified spectral-threshold OLS estimator over \(\|\beta\|_2\le B\) and the admissible conditional-noise class. Determine an explicit finite-\(n\) frontier separating regimes in which \(d^\star\) is minimax from regimes in which a nonuniform independent dosage has strictly smaller worst-case risk.
statements.justification: Population \(A\)-optimality does not settle the discontinuous finite-sample risk created by missing patterns and fallback bias.
statements.gap: ShyamalZhangUhler2025 proves only near-optimal bounds, and DerezinskiWarmuth2017 obtains exact inverse-Gram identities under a different dependent sampling law.
statements.consumer: The frontier would tell small interaction screens whether the asymptotically optimal uniform dosage is also the correct finite-budget design.

sampling_model.design: Choose \(d\in\mathcal D_L\); the focal design is \(d^\star=u\mathbf 1_p\).
sampling_model.treatment: Each unit receives mutually independent coordinates \(Z_{ai}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(d_i)\), coded as \(X_{ai}=2Z_{ai}-1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every dosage is interior; no claim is uniform as \(L\downarrow0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The chosen \(\Sigma_k(d^\star)\) is known from the randomization, so no nuisance is estimated.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For the additive model with \(k=1\), uniform limited-supply dosage is optimal up to a vanishing finite-sample factor.
Downward-closed hierarchical product designs satisfy an inverse-trace sum over products of marginal inverse-information excesses.
Matrix Chernoff bounds control both extreme eigenvalues of sums of independent bounded positive semidefinite matrices.
Random-design least-squares error separates covariance estimation, approximation, and response-noise contributions.
Volume sampling yields exact pseudoinverse expectations and an unbiased least-squares estimator under dependent subset sampling.

tldr: For independent product-Bernoulli assignment and the fixed complete Fourier basis through order \(k\), the population \(A\)-criterion is an explicit elementary-symmetric polynomial. Its unique shared-supply optimizer is the uniform dosage \(u=\min\{L/p,1/2\}\), with an exact criterion value and a sharp global quadratic stability certificate. Exact leverage, a rare-activation rank obstruction, and a two-sided risk theorem show when known-information spectral-threshold OLS attains the population oracle constant at fixed dimension. The product-design trace identity is classical and credited; the contribution is the constrained all-order corollary and its finite-sample package.

project_justification.gap: The modern PFED paper resolves limited supply analytically only for additive responses and reports numerical evidence for interaction models. Classical product-design theory gives the inverse-trace identity but not the shared expected-supply optimizer or the stated risk translation.
project_justification.niche: The fixed dosage-independent Fourier basis makes the criterion sensitive to marginal imbalance, while downward closure permits an exact orthonormal triangular reduction.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact all-order criterion, proves uniform dosage with a sharp global modulus, and couples it to exact leverage, rank-failure probability, and unconditional threshold-OLS risk.

related_work: Shyamal, Zhang, and Uhler introduce the same product-Bernoulli factorial model and bounded-order Fourier regression, but their limited-supply closed form is additive-only. Schwabe and Wong provide the classical downward-closed product-design inverse-trace identity that is specialized here, so that identity is not presented as new. Tropp supplies the matrix-Chernoff engine for the empirical Gram event. Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang motivate separating Gram conditioning from response noise in random-design regression. Dereziński and Warmuth show that exact inverse-Gram expectations are possible under volume sampling, a dependent design that is not compared as an admissible competitor. Freise and Schwabe and Ravichandran and coauthors study restricted factorial regions or cell allocations under dependent randomization rather than independent coordinate dosage. Yao and coauthors motivate high-multiplicity interaction screens, but their filtered guide-pooling implementation does not verify independent delivery or the homoskedastic Fourier regression used here.
technical_internal_limitation: At \(\beta=0\), spectral fallback can make finite-sample truncated risk smaller than the population \(A\)-risk. Thus the exact population optimizer is not asserted to minimize finite-sample risk over designs, and no minimax claim follows from the risk sandwich.
honest_scope: The exact population identity, optimizer, stability modulus, leverage, rank obstruction, and fixed-dimensional risk results are to be proved. Exact finite-sample minimax dosage remains open. The core excludes dependent or fixed-count assignment, growing dimension, heteroskedastic outcomes, adaptive rounds, model misspecification, and uniformity as supply vanishes. The Yao application is only an idealized consumer under independent delivery and the stated regression model.

seed_details.kernel: For the complete order-at-most-\(k\) Fourier model, derive the elementary-symmetric population \(A\)-criterion and prove the unique uniform shared-supply optimizer with an explicit sharp global curvature certificate.

seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Schwabe and Wong because their page-729 identity already gives the trace.
seed_details.rebuttal: The identity is fully credited; the unresolved content is the shared-supply simplex optimization, equality analysis, sharp curvature, leverage, and finite-sample attainment package. This limits the ambition to subfield.

seed_details.opened_anchor_receipt: The truncated-OLS construction, its conditional risk bounds, the passive half-dosage proof sketch, and the discussion of singular empirical Gram matrices were read from the arXiv source.
seed_details.kernel: At the exact population-optimal dosage, compute maximum whitened leverage and derive two-sided unconditional risk bounds, including the spectral-fallback bias, followed by uniform fixed-dimensional oracle attainment.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the \(\epsilon\)-net Gram bound by a rank-one matrix-Chernoff argument calibrated by exact Boolean leverage, then integrate the fallback branch rather than discarding it.
seed_details.target_method_search: Tropp gives the needed matrix lower and upper tails, and Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang decompose random-design regression error, but neither source treats activation-polynomial rank failures or the zero-fallback bias under product-Bernoulli Fourier sampling.

seed_details.rebuttal: The exact leverage envelope and discrete rank obstruction determine the supply-dependent scale; the unconditional two-sided decomposition exposes a bias term omitted by population \(A\)-risk comparisons.

literature_map.settled: PFED proves the limited-supply result only for the additive model and uses numerical optimization for interactions. Schwabe and Wong publish the downward-closed product inverse-trace identity. Restricted Hamming-region and randomization-allocation papers optimize different design classes or criteria.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: No located source combines the fixed dosage-independent complete order-at-most-\(k\) Fourier basis, independent Bernoulli coordinates, a shared expected-supply simplex, the exact optimizer, and a global stability modulus.
literature_map.closest_subsumption_check: Schwabe and Wong subsume the trace identity but not the shared-budget optimization or its equality and curvature certificate; therefore the identity is attributed and not claimed as novel.

literature_map.settled: Tropp supplies explicit rank-one matrix Chernoff tails. Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang isolate covariance, approximation, and noise error in random-design least squares. Dereziński and Warmuth obtain exact inverse-Gram expectations under dependent volume sampling.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: The exact product-Fourier leverage envelope, activation-polynomial rank obstruction, and unconditional zero-fallback bias decomposition are not supplied by these general results.
literature_map.closest_subsumption_check: PFED has truncated-risk bounds, but its limited-supply theorem stops at \(k=1\), and its concentration argument does not state the exact leverage-dependent all-\(k\) sandwich used here.

literature_map.settled: Near-optimality bounds and general regression decompositions do not identify the exact finite-sample minimax dosage. Exact pseudoinverse expectations are available for volume sampling, not for independent product sampling.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: The minimax saddle over dosage, coefficient ball, conditional noise, and threshold fallback remains open.
literature_map.closest_subsumption_check: A direct finite-support enumeration at \(\beta=0\) shows that truncated risk may lie below population \(A\)-risk, so the exact finite-risk problem cannot be inferred from population optimality.

novelty_justification: The trace identity is not novel: it is the Bernoulli specialization of Schwabe and Wong's downward-closed product-design formula. The narrow new kernel is the exact constrained corollary for the modern PFED model: the all-order shared-supply optimizer, its equality conditions and sharp global curvature certificate, the exact maximum leverage and discrete rank obstruction, and a leverage-calibrated two-sided unconditional risk theorem that retains the spectral-fallback bias. Shyamal, Zhang, and Uhler prove a limited-supply result only for \(k=1\) and report numerical evidence for interactions. No searched paper states this complete independent-product package. The scope is therefore subfield rather than field-level.
